sections.html:
Two neighboring suites in the Courthouse Annex on Tippins Street in Baxley divide the job. Suite 101 houses the Board of Tax Assessors, who put a value on your land and house. Suite 102 houses the Tax Commissioner, who sends the bill and collects payment.

A wrong turn costs you a trip. Take value questions, record errors, exemptions and appeals to the assessors. Take balances, payment options and back taxes to the tax commissioner. You can look up a parcel at qpublic.net/ga/appling, and the commissioner's page links to online payment.

The tax commissioner's counter is open weekdays, from 8 to 5. Liens against a parcel are recorded through the clerk, so Suite 103 matters when a county claim is attached to a house headed to market.

Appling County spreads across about 507 square miles of southeast Georgia. Baxley is both its seat and its biggest town. About 19,100 people live here, 3.5 percent more than in 2020. Owners hold 72.5 percent of households. A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $76,700, against median household income of $46,651. Only 21 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction rarely competes with a resale, and a seller here is mostly pricing against other older homes in town and the outlying farm roads. The county and the cities of Baxley, Graham and Surrency prepare a joint comprehensive plan, which is worth a look if you own land on the edge of town.

sections.h2: How a house is valued each year
sections.html:
The assessors set value as of January 1 and tax 40 percent of it. Take that assessed figure, subtract exemptions, and multiply by the millage rate. A mill equals a tenth of a cent per assessed dollar.

You may file a return from the start of the year to April 1, though you only need to when the parcel changed, say through a new building or extra acreage. Skipping a required return adds a 10 percent penalty on the unreported value and interest. Equipment and other personal property need a return each year by April 1.

Notices arrive in May. They list the value and carry an estimated bill using the previous year's rates, but the county tells owners this estimate is not a bill. The commissioners and school board have not finished budgets when the notice goes out, and millage usually gets set around September.

Georgia's default is December 20, with 60 days after billing to pay, yet your own bill's printed date is what counts. Most counties follow December 20.

The bill goes to the person who owned the house on New Year's Day. Even if you close in June, a statement can show up in fall for a home you no longer hold. Who actually pays is settled by your contract and the closing statement.

  • Pay in the tax commissioner's suite, by mail, or through the county's online portal.
  • Get any open year's payoff in writing before closing day.
  • A mobile home needs a location permit from the tax commissioner, applied for within 30 days of placing it and renewed every year before April 2.

Phone (912) 367-8105 to learn this year's bill date and what late charges apply.

Put the appeal on paper and bring it to Suite 101 within 45 days of the date printed on your notice. It has to be in hand by that day, and late filings are refused.

The tax rate cannot be appealed. Grounds are limited to taxability, value and uniformity, and you choose the path on state form PT-311A. Assessors get the first look. If the number stands, a Board of Equalization takes over, made up of citizens the grand jury appoints. You can pick arbitration instead, and a hearing officer is open only to non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000.

After a loss, a written notice for Superior Court must reach the assessors within 30 days after the decision is mailed or handed over. Before the court hears the case, state law requires payment of tax matching the last year in which tax was found due. The state revenue department has no power to overrule a local board on one parcel.

sections.h2: Can you claim a homestead exemption in Appling County?
sections.html:
Yes, for the home you legally live in. Here, unlike some counties, you apply at the Tax Assessors' office rather than with the tax commissioner.

Apply the year the house becomes your main residence, or up to April 1 of the next year. Once approved, it carries forward on its own unless you want to switch types. Appling has raised its local amounts above the state minimum, and the county tax page lists the standard exemption (S1) and a preferential assessment category. Ask the assessors at (912) 367-8108 for the current dollar amounts.

The savings belong to you, not the property. Your buyer must file separately, which means the first bill after closing will likely arrive without the exemption. The county commissioners also keep a posting about a school district ad valorem exemption on their meetings page.

Expect to pay it out of the proceeds. Unpaid tax follows the parcel, and a recorded county lien has to clear before the buyer gets clean title. Liens are filed with the clerk.

Each year's bill lands on the January 1 owner, and nothing is refunded for a partial year. Seller and buyer divide the year in the sales contract, and the closing attorney forwards the county's share. For an inherited house, the Probate Court on South Main Street handles the estate.

  • Get a payoff figure from Suite 102 for each year still open.
  • Search the clerk's files for liens on the parcel.
  • Put your latest assessment notice in the closing folder.
  • Read the settlement statement for a tax line before signing.

A cash buyer can close faster, but the payoff figures and lien check still come first. If you inherited the house, sort out the estate with the Probate Court before anyone signs a listing, since the buyer's attorney will ask who has authority to convey. Bring the death certificate and any court papers to the Baxley office, and ask the Tax Commissioner whether the bill is still in the decedent's name so the payoff letter shows the right owner.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Appling County tax bill online?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax commissioner's office points owners to a county online payment portal, and it also takes payments in person at Suite 102, 69 Tippins Street in Baxley, and by mail. The office phone is (912) 367-8105.

faqs.q: What fraction of market value does Appling County tax?
faqs.a: Forty percent of the January 1 fair market value. Exemptions come off that assessed figure first, then the millage rate is applied to what is left. One mill is $1 for every $1,000 of assessed value.

faqs.q: Is there any way to appeal after the notice period ends?
faqs.a: No. An appeal cannot be filed after the 45 days run out. The following year's notice brings the next chance, so note the deadline the day it arrives.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax in the year a house sells?
faqs.a: The owner at New Year is billed, but the sales contract can move the cost to the buyer for the months after closing. The closing attorney typically prorates the year and pays the county, so check that the settlement statement shows it.

faqs.q: Which phone number is for value questions?
faqs.a: Call (912) 367-8108, the Board of Tax Assessors, for values, records, appeals and exemptions. Dial the Tax Commissioner at (912) 367-8105 for billing and payments.
